topic: ICSE 10th Board Section A - Part 1: Multiple Choice Questions (Marks: 20)

questions.question: Which of the following data types represents a 32-bit single-precision floating-point number in Java?
questions.explanation: In Java, 'float' uses 32 bits (4 bytes) of IEEE 754 storage, whereas 'double' uses 64 bits.

questions.question: What is the return type of the method Character.isLetterOrDigit('9')?
questions.explanation: Character validation methods starting with 'is' evaluate whether the condition holds and return a primitive boolean.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to explicitly instantiate a new object or allocate array space in memory?
questions.explanation: The 'new' operator is dynamically executed at runtime to allocate memory on the heap for objects and arrays.

questions.question: What does Math.sqrt(0.25) evaluate to?
questions.explanation: Math.sqrt() returns the positive square root of a double value; the square root of 0.25 is 0.5.

questions.question: Which access modifier gives the least restrictive access, making members accessible from anywhere?
questions.explanation: The 'public' access specifier makes classes, methods, and variables accessible to all other classes across all packages.

questions.question: What is the result of the integer modulo operation 25 % 4?
questions.explanation: 25 divided by 4 leaves a quotient of 6 and a remainder of 1; the '%' operator captures the remainder.

questions.question: What is returned by the method call "PROGRAM".charAt(4)?
questions.explanation: Using 0-based indexing: 'P'(0), 'R'(1), 'O'(2), 'G'(3), 'R'(4). Index 4 maps to character 'R'.

questions.question: What is the term for passing an argument by passing a copy of its reference address?
questions.explanation: Java strictly uses call-by-value everywhere; when passing objects/arrays, a copy of the reference pointer is passed by value.

questions.question: Which of the following is an invalid variable name in Java?
questions.explanation: 'class' is a reserved Java keyword and cannot be used as an identifier.

questions.question: What will "EDUCATION".substring(2, 5) return?
questions.explanation: substring(2, 5) extracts characters from index 2 up to index 4 ('U', 'C', 'A').

questions.question: Which loop structure tests its condition after executing the body at least once?
questions.explanation: The 'do-while' loop is an exit-controlled loop that evaluates its conditional expression after executing the loop statements.

questions.question: What does Math.max(12.5, 12.51) return?
questions.explanation: Math.max() returns the algebraically larger value among two floating-point arguments, which is 12.51.

questions.question: What is the ASCII code value of the newline character ('\n')?
questions.explanation: In standard ASCII and Unicode tables, line feed / newline ('\n') corresponds to integer 10 (carriage return is 13).

questions.question: Which statement transfers control out of the enclosing loop or switch construct immediately?
questions.explanation: The 'break' statement terminates the active loop or switch block and resumes execution at the following statement.

questions.question: What is the return type of the method Character.toUpperCase(char ch)?
questions.explanation: Character.toUpperCase() converts the input character and returns its uppercase counterpart as a primitive char.

questions.question: What is the default initial value of an uninitialized element in a short array?
questions.explanation: All numeric integer-based arrays in Java (byte, short, int, long) default their unassigned slots to 0.

questions.question: What will Math.floor(-9.8) return?
questions.explanation: Math.floor() returns the largest mathematical double less than or equal to the argument; -10.0 is less than -9.8.

questions.question: Which String method replaces all instances of an old character with a new replacement character?
questions.explanation: The replace(char oldChar, char newChar) method returns a new String resulting from replacing all occurrences.

questions.question: Which operator represents the logical AND operation in Java?
questions.explanation: '&&' is the short-circuit logical AND operator used for evaluating boolean conditions.

questions.question: What does a method declaration require if it throws no values and does not return anything?
questions.explanation: The 'void' return type keyword indicates that a method performs actions without returning a calculated result.

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this single-character assignment:
options: char data type cannot hold multiple characters in single quotes
ch is an illegal variable identifier
questions.answer: char data type cannot hold multiple characters in single quotes
questions.explanation: A char literal stores exactly one 16-bit Unicode character; multi-letter literals must be enclosed in double quotes as Strings.

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this 2D Array allocation:
options: Array dimension capacity must be specified using square brackets [3][3], not parentheses (3)(3)
questions.answer: Array dimension capacity must be specified using square brackets [3][3], not parentheses (3)(3)
questions.explanation: Multidimensional arrays in Java strictly use square bracket pairs to indicate sizing and dimensions.

questions.question: Identify the logical flaw in this countdown loop:
options: i++ increments instead of decrementing (i--), causing an infinite loop
questions.answer: i++ increments instead of decrementing (i--), causing an infinite loop
questions.explanation: Incrementing i moves it further above 1, keeping the condition i >= 1 permanently true and triggering an infinite loop.

questions.question: Identify the library method error:
questions.code_snippet:
String msg = "Hello World";
int len = msg.length;
options: String uses the method length(), not the field property length
questions.answer: String uses the method length(), not the field property length
questions.explanation: Arrays use the length field property, whereas String objects require the invocation of length() with parentheses.

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this conditional equality check:
options: Comparison requires equality operator '==', not assignment '='
if condition must end with a semicolon
questions.answer: Comparison requires equality operator '==', not assignment '='
questions.explanation: A single '=' attempts value assignment inside the if condition, which is invalid since it evaluates to an integer rather than a boolean.

questions.question: Identify the logical error in this range-checking condition for positive numbers up to 100:
options: Requires logical AND (&&) instead of OR (||); current logic is unconditionally true for all numbers
questions.answer: Requires logical AND (&&) instead of OR (||); current logic is unconditionally true for all numbers
questions.explanation: Using OR (||) causes the check to match every possible number because any number is either greater than 0 or less than 100.

questions.question: Identify the library method error:
options: Method name must follow camelCase: valueOf()
questions.answer: Method name must follow camelCase: valueOf()
questions.explanation: Java methods strictly enforce camelCase naming; the correct method call is Integer.valueOf().

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this method signature:
options: Every formal parameter must specify its own explicit data type (int a, int b)
questions.answer: Every formal parameter must specify its own explicit data type (int a, int b)
questions.explanation: In Java method parameter lists, each variable must be declared with its own individual type specifier.

questions.question: Predict the output of the nested Math evaluation:

questions.explanation: Math.ceil(2.2) rounds up to 3.0. Math.floor(2.8) rounds down to 2.0. Adding them yields 5.0[cite: 1].
